standards: Every idea through the alpha gate

page.title: Research record
page.purpose: Every strategy we tested, how we tested it, and why only one book survived. Pick a strategy to see the test, the result and the reason.

headline.label: Deployed Trend+Carry book (v44 = v42 FINAL)
headline.note: Earlier vintages (v33 base book 1.03, v39 stack 1.25 at native vol) appear only inside their own study panels, each with its data vintage. Numbers differ across vintages because the price cache was re-downloaded between studies.

studies.title: The original S&P "TGA" engine
studies.hypothesis: Graph-topology and reversal signals on S&P 500 single names earn a daily edge.
studies.ask: Could a graph-and-reversal engine beat the S&P 500 on daily data?
studies.reason: Its result moved with the ticker list, so it isn't reproducible.

studies.title: Multi-sleeve re-measure
studies.hypothesis: Adding pairs and PEAD sleeves to the S&P engine lifts the combined book.
studies.ask: Did pairs and earnings drift add to the S&P book?
studies.reason: Voided: our simulator gave every short a phantom gain.

studies.title: Slow-book rebuild
studies.hypothesis: Vol-targeted momentum plus PEAD and a capped reversion leg make a viable S&P book.
studies.ask: Could a slower S&P book reach a Sharpe of 0.6?
studies.reason: Voided: five corrupted price days carried momentum.

studies.title: Clean-data sleeves and the earnings-drift beta test
studies.hypothesis: At least one S&P single-name sleeve has standalone alpha after costs.
studies.ask: On clean data, does any S&P stock sleeve earn alpha?
studies.reason: None did. The earnings-drift return was market exposure.

studies.title: Cross-asset time-series momentum
studies.hypothesis: Trend across ~23 liquid ETFs earns a positive, crisis-positive premium.
studies.ask: Does trend across asset classes pay, including in crises?
studies.reason: Sharpe 0.67, and +7.1% in 2008. It became the foundation.

studies.title: Carry / defensive sleeve and the blend
studies.hypothesis: A carry/defensive sleeve, risk-parity blended with trend, beats either alone.
studies.ask: Does a carry sleeve diversify trend?
studies.reason: Correlation +0.13 with trend; the blend became the flagship.

studies.title: Wiring Trend+Carry into paper trading
studies.hypothesis: The book can be paper-traded daily from a single source of truth.
studies.ask: Can the book paper-trade from the same code as the backtest?
studies.reason: Shipped. Backtest and live share one code path.

studies.title: Pairs as a third sleeve
studies.hypothesis: Cointegrated S&P pairs add an uncorrelated third sleeve to the book.
studies.ask: Do cointegrated pairs add a third sleeve?
studies.reason: Net Sharpe 0.24; filtering left little to trade.

studies.title: Flagship validation
studies.hypothesis: The base Trend+Carry book survives Monte Carlo, sensitivity and crisis tests.
studies.ask: Is the base book robust to resampling and setting changes?
studies.reason: Every check held. A bigger universe did worse.

studies.title: How the book works (leverage explainer)
studies.hypothesis: The book's Sharpe is invariant to the vol target; CAGR is a leverage dial.
studies.ask: How do return and drawdown scale with leverage?
studies.reason: Sharpe stays at 1.04 at every volatility target.

studies.title: Alpha gate, currency trend and meta-labeling
studies.hypothesis: An FX sleeve diversifies the book, and a meta-label model improves trend entries.
studies.ask: Does currency trend or a meta-label model help the book?
studies.reason: The small meta-label model passed; currency trend failed.

studies.title: LSTM features for the meta model
studies.hypothesis: LSTM-learned features or a vol forecaster lift the meta model.
studies.ask: Do LSTM features lift the meta-label model?
studies.reason: A small lift, from a network that had seen the future.

studies.title: LSTM, leak-free walk-forward
studies.hypothesis: The v36 LSTM lift survives when the LSTM is trained walk-forward.
studies.row_note: best leak-free variant; champion without LSTM 1.226
studies.ask: Does the LSTM lift survive walk-forward training?
studies.reason: No: Sharpe 1.222 with it, 1.226 without.

studies.title: Diversifiers and the regime de-risk overlay
studies.hypothesis: A new uncorrelated sleeve or a risk overlay improves the book.
studies.ask: Does a regime rule cut the book's drawdowns?
studies.reason: Worst drawdown −10.5% to −5.4%. New sleeves failed.

studies.title: Capstone validation and deployment
studies.hypothesis: The full stack (base → meta → regime → 8% vol) passes every gate together.
studies.ask: Does the whole stack pass as one system?
studies.reason: Passed and deployed. Calm-market leverage was rejected.

studies.title: Claude News Overlay (design)
studies.hypothesis: A pinned LLM reading point-in-time news can improve the regime de-risk.
studies.ask: Can a language model reading news improve the de-risk?
studies.reason: Built, then paused before any trial.

studies.title: Auditing our own live P&L
studies.hypothesis: The live paper-trading P&L measures the strategies, not the plumbing.
studies.ask: Were the live dashboard numbers right?
studies.reason: No. Accounting bugs fixed, tracks replayed, RL agent retired.

studies.title: Trend-signal refinements (Baltas–Kosowski)
studies.hypothesis: A t-statistic trend signal, range-based vol or a correlation factor improves the trend sleeve.
studies.ask: Do published trend-signal refinements improve the book?
studies.reason: Only the t-statistic signal passed. It cut trend turnover 20%.

studies.title: Replicating a published 49%-a-year stat-arb
studies.hypothesis: Graph-clustered intra-cluster reversal (SPONGE + classifier) earns the published return.
studies.row_note: paper-faithful R1 shown; the realistic R4 never traded
studies.ask: Does a published 49%-a-year stat-arb replicate?
studies.reason: No. It traded on 4 of 228 rebalances.

studies.title: Promoting the t-statistic signal and rebuilding the paper track
studies.hypothesis: The v42 TREND signal can go live without changing anything else in the book.
studies.ask: Can the new trend signal go live without breaking anything?
studies.reason: Deployed; the paper track restarted under the new book.

studies.title: A second battery in California
studies.hypothesis: The ERCOT battery's forecast and dispatch rules earn a diversifying return on CAISO too.
studies.vintage: frozen walk-forward forecasts, local days 2025-10-12 to 2026-06-27 (251 days)
studies.row_note: CAISO net Sharpe on daily $/MW P&L; not comparable with the ETF books
studies.ask: Does the battery rule work on a second grid?
studies.reason: CAISO passed its inclusion rule. See the v47 caveat.

studies.title: Agricultural curve premia on free data
studies.hypothesis: The change in an agricultural futures curve's slope predicts returns beyond plain momentum.
studies.vintage: Yahoo futures and fund prices downloaded 2026-10-18, 2011-07-05 to 2026-10-16
studies.ask: Do agricultural curve premia work on free data?
studies.reason: No contract data; the proxy only matched plain momentum.

studies.title: Does the battery forecast beat simple price shapes?
studies.hypothesis: The day-ahead price forecast captures more of perfect insight than simple price shapes planned the same way.
studies.vintage: frozen walk-forward forecasts, 2025-10-12 to 2026-06-27, point-in-time weather
studies.row_note: capture of perfect insight; no Sharpe
studies.ask: Does the battery forecast beat simple price shapes?
studies.reason: No. A 14-day average shape beat it on both grids.

studies.title: Timing the VIX futures premium
studies.hypothesis: A steep VIX futures curve (front above spot) forecasts weak VX futures returns after the 2014 publication.
studies.vintage: VX settlements built from Cboe daily files through 2026-10-16
studies.row_note: killed at the kill test before any trading rule ran; no Sharpe
studies.ask: Does the VIX futures basis still predict returns?
studies.reason: No. The slope turned positive after 2014.

studies.title: VIX curve inversion as a de-risk trigger
studies.hypothesis: Front-month VIX futures above the second month is a better de-risk signal than SPY's trend and volatility.
studies.ask: Is VIX curve inversion a better de-risk trigger?
studies.reason: No. Sharpe 1.24 to 1.12, and turnover tripled.

studies.title: Treasury auction cycle and the month-end bond trade
studies.hypothesis: Treasury ETFs cheapen before auctions and recover after, and long bonds earn a premium over month-end.
studies.row_note: stopped at the per-round-trip kill test; no Sharpe
studies.ask: Do Treasury auctions or month-ends pay in ETFs?
studies.reason: Both below the bars set in advance.
